tools.name: get_started_guide
tools.description: Returns a role-scoped welcome message and curated sample questions to help you get started with DeskMonitor AI. Use when a new user asks 'what can I do?', 'what can I ask?', or 'how do I get started?' Call this first when connecting. Do NOT use for querying live workforce data.

tools.name: get_data_dictionary
tools.description: Returns the schema of queryable data — what fields exist, their meaning, and which tools expose them. Includes the RetentionPolicy entity — how long screenshots and monitoring data are kept per plan. Use when the user asks 'what data exists?', 'what fields are available?', 'what is a productivity sc

tools.name: switch_to_demo
tools.description: Switches to DeskMonitor demo mode with synthetic data. Returns demo tenant info and suggested queries. Use when the user wants to explore without a real account. Use a dm_demo_* API key to call data tools in demo mode.

tools.name: switch_to_production
tools.description: Switches back to production mode and confirms your real tenant context from your auth token. Use when the user wants to see their real company data after exploring demo mode.

tools.name: get_demo_scenarios
tools.description: Returns 5 guided scenario walkthroughs using the demo tenant's synthetic data. Use when the user wants to see example queries or guided tours of DeskMonitor capabilities.

tools.name: get_dashboard_summary
tools.description: Returns the dashboard KPIs for the current user — hours worked today, team productivity score, pending approvals, active headcount. Use when the user asks 'how is my team today?', 'am I clocked in?', 'what's my summary?'. Do NOT use for historical timesheet data — use list_my_timesheet for that.

tools.name: list_employees
tools.description: Lists employees visible to the current user based on their role. Supports pagination and name search. Use when the user asks 'who is on my team?', 'list all employees', or wants a roster. Use get_employee_details for information about ONE specific person.

tools.name: get_employee_details
tools.description: Returns the full profile for a specific employee including role, team, clock-in status, and recent activity. Use when the user asks about ONE specific person. Use list_employees for multiple people. Use 'me' as employee_id for the authenticated user's own profile.

tools.name: list_my_timesheet
tools.description: Returns the authenticated user's time log entries for a date range. Use when the user asks 'how many hours have I worked?', 'show me my timesheet', or 'what did I work on yesterday?'. Cannot query another person's timesheet — use summarize_team_hours for team-level hours.

tools.name: summarize_team_hours
tools.description: Aggregates hours worked by the manager's team for a given period. Requires Manager role or above. Use when the manager asks 'how many hours did my team work this week?', 'show me team hours', or 'who worked the most hours?'. Do NOT use for an individual employee's timesheet — use list_my_timesheet f

tools.name: list_pending_approvals
tools.description: Returns timesheets pending approval in the manager's team. Requires Manager role or above. Use when the manager asks 'show me pending approvals', 'who needs sign-off?', or 'any outstanding timesheets?'. Read-only -- this tool LISTS pending items only; it cannot approve them. tools.name: list_recent_activity
tools.description: Returns a daily aggregate activity feed scoped to the authenticated user, including clock events, timesheet submissions, and approval actions. tools.name: get_workload_alerts
tools.description: Returns workload alerts — team members with unusual hours, employees not yet clocked in, timesheet gaps. Use when the manager asks 'who needs attention?', 'any anomalies today?', 'any warnings?', or 'are there any issues?'.

tools.name: get_productivity_overview
tools.description: Returns productivity scores and active/idle time ratios for an employee or team. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "v1" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_started_guide, list_recent_activity, get_workload_alerts, get_productivity_overview, get_capabilities, get_pricing_and_plans, start_free_trial, ask_workforce · Private data: switch_to_demo, switch_to_production, clock_in, clock_out, get_pricing_and_plans, get_analytics_overview, get_analytics_feature_usage · Public sink: invite_staff.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_started_guide, list_recent_activity, get_workload_alerts, get_productivity_overview, get_capabilities, get_pricing_and_plans, start_free_trial, ask_workforce · Private data: switch_to_demo, switch_to_production, clock_in, clock_out, get_pricing_and_plans, get_analytics_overview, get_analytics_feature_usage · Public sink: invite_staff

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
